plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of pale, almost white-pink blossoms cover bare branches before the leaves appear. Petals drift down like confetti in spring breezes. Parks and riverbanks fill with picnickers for hanami, the Japanese tradition of flower viewing.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April in Japan. Flowering typically begins in Tokyo around March 20-25.
plants.location: Tokyo and the Kanto region, Japan, plus Washington, D.C., where peak bloom usually falls in late March to early April
plants.funFact: Nearly every Yoshino cherry tree is a clone grafted from a single original tree. That is why trees in the same area tend to bloom within days of each other.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding trumpets of golden yellow, ringed by paler petals, light up woodland floors and meadows. In the cool, damp days of early spring they appear in drifts that can look like pools of sunshine under still-bare trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February to April in the Northern Hemisphere. March is typically the peak in Britain.
plants.location: Woodlands and meadows of western Europe, including England, Wales and France
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain toxic alkaloids, which is why deer and rabbits leave them alone. One of those compounds, galantamine, has been used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.
